execute-plan.md.reason: #3830 makes `state.advance-plan` REFUSE to advance when `## Current Position` disagrees with the plans on disk, and the refusal reaches stdout at exit 0. This step ran the verb bare, discarded stdout and never tested the exit code, so the refusal was a silent non-write: progress was recalculated and a metric recorded for a plan that was never advanced past. The growth is the guard plus the reasoning that has to travel with it, because this is shipped shell read by an agent at runtime rather than by a compiler. Three things are load-bearing and each cost a wrong draft before it was written down: the arms are an ALLOW-LIST (`advanced: true`, or `advanced: false` WITH `reason: last_plan`) rather than a deny-list on the known refusals, because a deny-list writes on every answer shape the caller has not been taught -- a crashed gsd_run leaving the capture empty, and any refusal reason the verb grows later; the discriminator is never `advanced` alone, since `advanced: false` is also the ordinary last-plan answer and branching on it would skip the final plan's recording on every phase; and the prose note beneath the fence is not decoration, because a `case` arm suppresses only its own block and cannot stop the fenced block that follows. No prose was moved into an eagerly @-imported reference to shrink the measured file -- total loaded context grew by exactly this diff.

gsd-executor.md.reason: The same guard, in the second caller. The #3862 review named `workflows/execute-plan.md` as the sole in-repo caller; a recursive sweep found this file executing the verb too, so it carries the same three-arm allow-list and the same halt instruction -- here also covering the ROADMAP/requirements block that follows. Growth was deliberately held to 1,816 bytes against the 49,152-byte LARGE tier cap in tests/agent-size-budget.test.cjs (49,062 now, 90 under): an earlier draft crossed it at 49,859, and the remedy was removing the ~1,200 bytes of rationale this file had been duplicating from execute-plan.md rather than raising the cap, which that test calls a red line in as many words. What remains here is the trap itself; the long-form argument lives in the changeset and the PR body. No prose was moved into an eagerly @-imported reference to shrink the measured file.
